title: Personnel field suppression contract
reconstructedFrom: INS-18 report revision 3, sections 15-21. The spike that first emitted this file (spikes/ins18-lineage/out/field-suppression.v3.json) is not present on any checkout, so the nine rules are re-expressed here from the report that specifies them, and committed so the data-access layer reads a version-controlled input rather than an artifact that can disappear.
enforcementPoint: src/lib/data/personnel-projection.js — the select list and the cited projection. A suppressed column is never fetched, so it cannot reach a template, a schema.org graph, a data- attribute, or an inline prefill payload.
insufficientEnforcementPoints: A template guard. It hides a value from the visible DOM and still ships it in the page source, in prefill payloads and in structured data (INS-18 section 4b).
A column-level rule alone. Badge numbers also publish inside narrative prose, where dropping a column does not reach them (INS-18 section 16).

rules.reason: The TCOLE public-records production has four sheets and 31 columns and no badge-number column anywhere. Badge is not a field awaiting provenance work; the only established channel cannot ever supply it. All 7 badge values in the corpus are hand-authored, 4 of them attached to a person we label Unknown, and one (49112) is a squad-car number the seed's own narrative calls a vehicle number. A wrong badge number routes a real allegation onto the wrong human being.
rules.decidedBy: INS-11 section 3; deploy condition on INS-34

rules.reason: Suppressing agency_personnel.badge_number does not touch badge numbers published inside prose. One civil_cases row publishes three officer badge numbers in its claims summary. A field-level rule is required, not only a column rule.
rules.evidence: INS-18 report rev 3 section 16, 'Column suppression does not suppress the field'

rules.reason: 110 live profiles are hand-authored with no source dataset. They need no enumeration: a row that no attestation covers is not_traceable by default, and default-deny is what makes the rule survive new rows nobody told us about.
rules.evidence: INS-18 report rev 3 sections 14, 17 and 20 correction 2
rules.decidedBy: INS-10 — render provenance only where lineage is demonstrable, suppress the field otherwise

rules.reason: TCOLE uses in-band placeholders in SFX: 27 'N/A', 9 'n/a', one '1'. We published them verbatim as name suffixes on 37 live pages, including in the page title and baked into the canonical URL. A placeholder is not a fact about a person. Only the fields with a genuinely closed vocabulary get the full list: a prefix, a suffix and a job title cannot be 'None' or '0', but a middle name can, so middle name is narrowed to the literal 'NULL' that the production carries 10,340 times as its own placeholder. A token sweep across every name field would unpublish real people — Null, None and Na are real name components held by real officers.
rules.evidence: INS-18 report rev 3 section 18 item 2; narrowing per field follows the measurement on INS-69 (PR #18)
rules.decidedBy: accuracy; engineering call recorded on INS-10

rules.reason: Five people with the surname True broke the identity mapper, which coerced the string to a boolean and wrote 1. A name column holding a coerced boolean publishes a wrong name about a real person, and a provenance gate alone passes it because the lineage is perfect. The tokens are the coercion artifacts only — '1' and '0'. They are deliberately NOT 'True', 'False', 'Null' or 'NaN': those are real surnames and name fragments held by real officers in this corpus, and matching them would unpublish the very people this rule exists to protect. The five known coerced rows are withheld by slug under traceable-but-not-correct, which is evidence rather than a guess. Generally: name columns must be read as text and never coerced.
rules.evidence: INS-18 report rev 3 section 18 items 3 and 4; token list narrowed to the measurement on INS-69 (PR #18); generalised on INS-68
rules.decidedBy: accuracy; engineering call recorded on INS-10

rules.reason: 117 assignment rows carry start_date 1970-01-01 and 102 publish. The cause is in the seed: hand-authored rows for people whose start date is unknown, with NOT NULL forbidding the honest value. The sentinel is a missing value wearing a date.
rules.evidence: INS-18 report rev 3 sections 5 and 18 item 6
rules.decidedBy: accuracy; engineering call recorded on INS-10

rules.reason: No attested retrieval date exists for any row by any load path. manifest.json records processed_at_utc, which is the date we processed the file, not the date the agency produced it. An attestation that names a source, names a dataset and verifies a hash is still not traceable, and no configuration may promote it. Rendering is allowed at this class, but the citation states that the retrieval date is unattested.
rules.evidence: INS-18 report rev 3 sections 0 and 15; blocker carried on INS-64
rules.decidedBy: INS-18; enforced in classify() in provenance.ts

rules.reason: These records reproduce the source production exactly and are still wrong on the page: one is a TCOLE test record published as a human being; five had a surname deleted by a NULL-literal collision where Null may be the real surname; five carry a boolean coerced from the surname True. Provenance and accuracy are different properties and a provenance gate alone passes every one of them. The surname question is a genuine source ambiguity for TCOLE to answer, not for an automated cleanup to guess.
rules.evidence: INS-18 report rev 3 section 18 items 1, 3 and 4
rules.decidedBy: INS-68 owns the page-level remediation; the field-level withholding is this contract's

rules.reason: Identity resolution is name-based: 124,383 unique-name matches, 5,579 resolved by service history, 6 decided by arbitrary duplicate ordering, and nothing records which 6. A per-row citation that hides a name collision claims more than we measured, so the collision tier is disclosed to the reader. The 6 rows whose match was decided by row order are not a match at all and are withheld.
rules.decidedBy: INS-18 requirement carried to INS-5; tier split is an engineering call recorded on INS-10
